doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How Coltrane introduced new tunes without charts
summary: Trane played tunes for the band, no charts, and the rhythm section listened until it could play; Elvin changed rhythms freely.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When one listens to the music the quartet was performing it sounds, at many times, like its equal participation. Of course there is a definite dialogue between you and Trane. So how did Trane as the bandleader, say if he introduced a new song, how would the band deal with that, negotiate the new song? How was that introduced?
Well he was always bringing up new tunes. First of all you have to listen till you can hear it and then you have to play until you can play it. It’s as simple as that.
So when you say listen, so Trane would come in and play it first and then play it for the other band members
Yeah and then you begin to understand, and feel what the music is all about. Cause there is no title, there isn’t—the only time I saw a name for tunes was on the record jacket
Did he ever come in with anything written?
Not even for McCoy or Jimmy?
I supposed he talk to them. He had conversations with McCoy at different times. I’m sure he must have mentioned to them what he wanted. It was always more or less very personal.
Did you also make suggestions in the process? Did the other member make suggestions or was it more musical rather than verbal?

I never made any suggestions. I would change a rhythm sometimes and it would fit with what that melodic line was at that moment. So having the freedom to do that is an accomplishment in itself. Most bands don’t have that type of confidence that they can just play freely but that’s the way we did it.
Did you as the rhythm section, you, McCoy, and Jimmy, did you ever talk about what you were doing or what you would be doing?
No. I just tried to hear 'em. When they were playing I would listen very closely to what they were doing and try to enhance it. If not I’d leave it alone.
